analysis:
This batch contains documentation only. It adds changelog.d/gptoss-bf16-activations.md (head lines 1-22) and changes one table row in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (line 97 on base and head).

The changelog describes a code change that is not part of this batch. The GPT-OSS SwiGLU clamp bounds now use the activation dtype, so bf16 activations and KV are kept on every layer. As a result:
- The KV bytes per token are halved.
- The heartbeat field kv_bytes_per_token halves.
- Output is not bit-identical to the float32 path (T-007/T-027 concern only correctness, not attestation).
- Float32-typed SSD complete checkpoints fall into a different namespace and are not restored; they expire under the existing 30-minute TTL.

On T-041, the changelog says checkpoint identity already includes the observed native K/V types. A layer-dtype change therefore fails closed to a cold prefill rather than restoring incompatible state. No HMAC naming, AAD, salt scoping or TTL change is described.

The hardware-support.md edit only notes that the 3.5 GiB gpt-oss-20b activation floor was measured on the float32 path and has not been re-measured with bf16. bf16 activations should use less memory, so the old floor is plausibly conservative. Even so, the availability assumption (T-029/T-016 class) is unverified until re-measured.

Integration should check the following in the actual Swift change, which is not supplied here:
- The clamp dtype change in the GPT-OSS model code.
- That the checkpoint namespace or identity truly includes the per-layer dtype, so no cross-dtype restore is possible.
- That admission and paged sizing read the observed dtype rather than an assumed one.
- That the halved kv_bytes_per_token stays compatible with coordinator servability and admission (platform-owned).

No security regression is identifiable from documentation alone.
